intro: Hi! In Indonesian you say things like 'Rumah ini dibangun tahun 1990' and 'HP-ku dicuri!' all the time. English has the same idea, the passive: This house was built in 1990. My phone was stolen! Today you build it with is/are/was/were + the third form, say who did it with by, and learn when it's the better choice. Warm-up: where were you born? (I was born in…: you already use a passive!)
teachingNotes: Form: the passive is be + the third form (past participle), with the thing that receives the action as the subject. This lesson teaches two tenses only: present simple passive am/is/are + third form (routines, facts, processes: The rooms are cleaned every morning. Rice is grown in Java.) and past simple passive was/were + third form (finished events: My phone was stolen. These houses were built in 2010.). be agrees with the new subject (is/are, was/were) and shows the time; the third form never changes. Negatives and questions work like be: isn't/wasn't + third form; Is breakfast included? Was it built…? Don't teach the present perfect passive (has been done), the continuous passive (is being cleaned), will be / can be + third form, or get-passives; if the learner asks, say they come later.

Bridge from Indonesian: di- verbs (dibangun, dicuci, dibersihkan, dijual, dikirim, ditulis, dicuri, ditanam) are a good map: di- ≈ be + third form, and oleh ≈ by. But di- shows neither time nor number, so English must choose is/are/was/were. Learners already know one passive as a phrase: I was born in… (Indonesian lahir is active, so watch for *'I born in Medan').

Common error 1: no be. *'The office cleaned every day' → 'The office is cleaned every day.' Explain why: without be, 'cleaned' reads as the past simple, so the sentence says the office did the cleaning. Also contrast with the present continuous they know: is + -ing = the subject does it now (Rina is cleaning the room); is + third form = it happens to the subject (The room is cleaned every day). *'The room is cleaning' is wrong.

Common error 2: the past instead of the third form. *'This house was build in 1990' → 'was built'; also *'was wrote', *'were took', *'was stole', *'was builded'. Known third forms from A2: seen, been, eaten, gone, done, written, taken, had, bought, made, said, + regular -ed. New in this lesson (teach as words to remember): built, paid, sold, sent (third form = past), grown, stolen, spoken, given (new third form).

Common error 3: *'The novel was written from Pramoedya' → 'by Pramoedya'. by = oleh (who did the action); from = dari (where something comes from: a letter from Budi, made in Japan). After by use the object form: by me, him, her, us, them. made by = the maker (made by my grandmother), made in = the place (made in Pekalongan).

When to use it: the doer is unknown (My wallet was stolen), obvious (The rubbish is collected on Mondays: rubbish is British, Americans say trash or garbage), or unimportant, or the thing is the topic (Rice is grown in Java; processes, notices, news). Leave out by + someone/people when it adds nothing. Use the active when the doer matters, especially I: *'The coffee was made by me' sounds strange → 'I made the coffee'. Indonesian 'Kopinya saya buat' is a passive, but English prefers the active with I. In checkpoint questions where both forms are grammatical, ask for the passive (or the active) explicitly.

keyPoints.title: be + the third form
keyPoints.explanation: The passive starts with the thing that receives the action: The office is cleaned every day (dibersihkan). Present simple passive: am/is/are + third form, for routines and facts. Past simple passive: was/were + third form, for finished events. Choose is/are or was/were by the new subject and the time. Don't drop be ('The office cleaned' says the office did the cleaning), and use the third form, not the past: was built, not 'was build'.

examples.en: The rooms are cleaned every morning.

id.title: be + bentuk ketiga
id.explanation: Passive dimulai dengan benda yang dikenai tindakan: The office is cleaned every day (dibersihkan). Present simple passive: am/is/are + bentuk ketiga, untuk kebiasaan dan fakta. Past simple passive: was/were + bentuk ketiga, untuk kejadian yang sudah selesai. Pilih is/are atau was/were sesuai subjek barunya dan waktunya. Jangan buang be ('The office cleaned' berarti kantornya yang membersihkan), dan pakai bentuk ketiga, bukan bentuk lampau: was built, bukan 'was build'.

keyPoints.title: by + the doer
keyPoints.explanation: To say who did the action, add by + the doer after the verb: The novel was written by Pramoedya. by = oleh. Don't use from (dari): from says where something comes from (a letter from Budi), not who did it. After by, use me, him, her, us, them.

examples.en: Bumi Manusia was written by Pramoedya Ananta Toer.
examples.id: Bumi Manusia ditulis oleh Pramoedya Ananta Toer.

examples.en: The new office was designed by a team from Bandung.
examples.id: Kantor baru itu dirancang oleh tim dari Bandung.

examples.en: The cake was made by her.

id.title: by + pelaku
id.explanation: Untuk menyebut siapa yang melakukan tindakan, tambahkan by + pelaku setelah kata kerjanya: The novel was written by Pramoedya. by = oleh. Jangan pakai from (dari): from menunjukkan asal sesuatu (a letter from Budi), bukan siapa pelakunya. Setelah by, pakai me, him, her, us, them.

keyPoints.title: When the passive is better
keyPoints.explanation: Use the passive when the doer is unknown (My phone was stolen), obvious (The rubbish is collected on Mondays) or unimportant, or when the thing is the topic (Rice is grown in Java). Then you usually leave out by. Use the active when the doer matters, especially when it's you: I made the coffee, not 'The coffee was made by me'.

examples.en: My phone was stolen on the bus.
Rice is grown in many parts of Java.
examples.id: Padi ditanam di banyak daerah di Jawa.

id.title: Kapan passive lebih tepat
id.explanation: Pakai passive kalau pelakunya tidak diketahui (My phone was stolen), sudah jelas (The rubbish is collected on Mondays) atau tidak penting, atau kalau bendanya yang jadi topik (Rice is grown in Java). Biasanya by tidak perlu disebut. Pakai kalimat aktif kalau pelakunya penting, terutama kalau pelakunya kamu sendiri: I made the coffee, bukan 'The coffee was made by me'.

assessment.prompt: Complete with the present simple passive of 'sell': KRL tickets ___ at every station.
assessment.rubric: Correct: are sold. 'is sold' = 60 (tickets is plural → are). 'are sell' or 'are selled' = 40 (needs the third form: sell → sold → sold). 'were sold' = 50 (a fact about now → present). 'sold' alone = 20 (missing be: the tickets don't sell anything).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the past simple passive of 'send': The invoices ___ to the client yesterday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: were sent. 'was sent' = 60 (invoices is plural → were). 'were send' or 'were sended' = 40 (needs the third form sent). 'are sent' = 40 (yesterday → past). 'sent' alone = 20 (missing be).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake (it's a fact about now): Our office cleaned every evening.
acceptableAnswers: our office is cleaned every evening
assessment.rubric: Correct: Our office is cleaned every evening (be is missing: the office doesn't clean, it is cleaned). 'Our office was cleaned every evening' = 60 (grammatical, but the task says it's a fact about now). 'Our office is cleaning every evening' = 20 (is + -ing says the office does the cleaning). 'Our office are cleaned' = 60. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Translate with 'by': Foto ini diambil oleh Budi.
acceptableAnswers: this photo was taken by budi
this picture was taken by budi
this photograph was taken by budi
assessment.rubric: Correct: This photo was taken by Budi. 'This photo is taken by Budi' = 50 (the photo was taken at a finished time → was). 'was took' = 40 (past form instead of the third form taken). 'taken from Budi' = 40 (oleh = by; from = dari). 'Budi took this photo' = 50 (right meaning, but the task asks for the passive with by). 'This photo taken by Budi' = 40 (missing was).

assessment.prompt: Correct the mistake: The new company logo was designed from Dimas.
acceptableAnswers: the new company logo was designed by dimas
assessment.rubric: Correct: The new company logo was designed by Dimas (the doer goes after by = oleh; from = dari is for where something comes from). 'Dimas designed the new company logo' = 60 (correct English, but the task is to fix the passive). 'designed with Dimas' = 20. Sentence unchanged = 0.

assessment.prompt: Nobody knows who did it. Rewrite in the passive, without the doer: Someone stole my wallet on the KRL.
acceptableAnswers: my wallet was stolen on the krl
assessment.rubric: Correct: My wallet was stolen on the KRL. 'My wallet was stolen by someone on the KRL' = 70 (grammatical, but by someone adds nothing: the doer is unknown, and the task asks to leave it out). 'My wallet was stole' = 40 (past form instead of the third form stolen). 'My wallet is stolen' = 40 (a finished event → was). 'My wallet stolen' = 30 (missing was).

assessment.prompt: This sounds strange because the doer is 'me'. Rewrite it in the active: The coffee was made by me this morning.
acceptableAnswers: i made the coffee this morning
this morning i made the coffee
assessment.rubric: Correct: I made the coffee this morning (when the doer is you, English uses the active, even though Indonesian says 'Kopinya saya buat'). 'I make the coffee this morning' = 50 (this morning, finished → made). 'I was made the coffee' = 10 (mixes passive and active). 'I made coffee this morning' = 90. Sentence unchanged = 0.

blocks.text:
Compare: *Pak Joko cleans the office every day* and *The office is cleaned every day*. The second sentence is **passive**: it starts with the thing that **receives** the action (the office), not the person who does it. You know this from Indonesian: *Pak Joko membersihkan kantor* → *Kantor **di**bersihkan setiap hari*.

**di- ≈ be + the third form** (bentuk ketiga, the **past participle**, which you met in the present perfect).
- **Present simple passive: am/is/are + third form**, for routines, facts and processes: *The office **is cleaned** every day.*
- **Past simple passive: was/were + third form**, for finished events: *This house **was built** in 1990.*

Indonesian *di-* never shows **when** or **how many**, but English has to choose: **is/are** (now, always) or **was/were** (finished), and singular or plural for the **new subject** (subjek = the word before the verb, here the thing).

id.text:
Bandingkan: *Pak Joko cleans the office every day* dan *The office is cleaned every day*. Kalimat kedua adalah **passive** (kalimat pasif): kalimatnya dimulai dengan benda yang **dikenai** tindakan (kantornya), bukan orang yang melakukannya. Kamu sudah kenal ini dari bahasa Indonesia: *Pak Joko membersihkan kantor* → *Kantor **di**bersihkan setiap hari*.

**di- ≈ be + bentuk ketiga** (dalam bahasa Inggris disebut **past participle**, yang sudah kamu pelajari di present perfect).
- **Present simple passive: am/is/are + bentuk ketiga**, untuk kebiasaan, fakta dan proses: *The office **is cleaned** every day.*
- **Past simple passive: was/were + bentuk ketiga**, untuk kejadian yang sudah selesai: *This house **was built** in 1990.*

*di-* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah menunjukkan **kapan** atau **berapa banyak**, tapi bahasa Inggris harus memilih: **is/are** (sekarang, selalu) atau **was/were** (sudah selesai), dan tunggal atau jamak sesuai **subjek baru** (subjek = kata sebelum kata kerja, di sini bendanya).

rows.en: The rooms are cleaned every morning.
This dish is called rendang.
These houses were built in 2010.
Borobudur was built in the 9th century.
Is breakfast included? — No, it isn't.
rows.note: question: be first; negative: isn't + third form

id.note: pertanyaan: be di depan; negatif: isn't + bentuk ketiga

blocks.text: You already use a passive: **I was born in Medan** (born is the third form of an old verb, *bear*: just remember it as a phrase). Indonesian *lahir* has no di-, so learners often say 'I born in Medan'. English needs **was**: I **was** born, she **was** born, they **were** born.

id.text: Kamu sebenarnya sudah memakai passive: **I was born in Medan** (born adalah bentuk ketiga dari kata kerja lama, *bear*: hafalkan saja sebagai ungkapan). *Lahir* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak memakai di-, jadi pelajar sering bilang 'I born in Medan'. Bahasa Inggris perlu **was**: I **was** born, she **was** born, they **were** born.

blocks.prompt: The rooms at this hotel ___ every morning.
blocks.explain: The rooms don't clean anything: someone cleans them, every morning → are + third form: are cleaned. 'clean' says the rooms do the cleaning, and 'are cleaning' (be + -ing) says they are doing it right now.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The rooms at this hotel ___ every morning.
id.explain: Kamarnya tidak membersihkan apa-apa: ada orang yang membersihkannya, setiap pagi → are + bentuk ketiga: are cleaned. 'clean' berarti kamarnya yang membersihkan, dan 'are cleaning' (be + -ing) berarti kamarnya sedang membersihkan sekarang.

material.title: Two traps: no be, and the wrong form

blocks.text:
**Trap 1: forgetting be.** *Kantor dibersihkan setiap hari* has one word for the verb, so learners write 'The office cleaned every day'. But without be, **cleaned** looks like the past simple, and the sentence says the **office** did the cleaning. The office doesn't clean: it **is cleaned**. Indonesian *di-* does the job that **be** does in English, so you need both parts: **is + cleaned**.

Don't mix it up with the present continuous: **is + -ing** = the subject does it (*Rina is cleaning the room*); **is + third form** = it happens to the subject (*The room is cleaned every day*).

**Trap 2: the past instead of the third form.** After be you need the **third form**: 'This house was build' (base form) and 'The letter was wrote' (past form) are wrong → **was built**, **was written**. Regular verbs are easy (third form = past: *cleaned, designed*). These irregular verbs are new: learn them as words to remember.

id.text:
**Jebakan 1: lupa be.** *Kantor dibersihkan setiap hari* hanya punya satu kata kerja, jadi pelajar menulis 'The office cleaned every day'. Tapi tanpa be, **cleaned** terlihat seperti past simple, dan kalimatnya berarti **kantornya** yang membersihkan. Kantor tidak membersihkan: kantor **is cleaned** (dibersihkan). *di-* dalam bahasa Indonesia melakukan tugas yang dilakukan **be** dalam bahasa Inggris, jadi kamu perlu dua-duanya: **is + cleaned**.

Jangan tertukar dengan present continuous: **is + -ing** = subjeknya yang melakukan (*Rina is cleaning the room*); **is + bentuk ketiga** = subjeknya yang dikenai (*The room is cleaned every day*).

**Jebakan 2: bentuk lampau, bukan bentuk ketiga.** Setelah be kamu perlu **bentuk ketiga**: 'This house was build' (bentuk dasar) dan 'The letter was wrote' (bentuk lampau) itu salah → **was built**, **was written**. Kata kerja beraturan itu mudah (bentuk ketiga = bentuk lampau: *cleaned, designed*). Kata kerja tidak beraturan di bawah ini baru: hafalkan saja.

rows.en: build → built → built
pay → paid → paid
sell → sold → sold
send → sent → sent
grow → grew → grown
steal → stole → stolen
speak → spoke → spoken
give → gave → given

blocks.text: Third forms you already know from the present perfect work here too: **seen, eaten, done, written, taken, bought, made, said**. Only **be** changes for the time and the subject; the third form never changes: *The bill **is** paid. The bills **were** paid.*

id.text: Bentuk ketiga yang sudah kamu kenal dari present perfect juga dipakai di sini: **seen, eaten, done, written, taken, bought, made, said**. Hanya **be** yang berubah sesuai waktu dan subjeknya; bentuk ketiganya tidak pernah berubah: *The bill **is** paid. The bills **were** paid.*

blocks.explain: A finished event and one school → was, then the third form: build → built → built. 'was build' uses the base form, and 'built' alone says the school built something.

id.explain: Kejadian yang sudah selesai dan satu sekolah → was, lalu bentuk ketiga: build → built → built. 'was build' memakai bentuk dasar, dan 'built' saja berarti sekolahnya yang membangun sesuatu.

id.title: Dua jebakan: tanpa be, dan bentuk yang salah

blocks.text:
Usually a passive sentence doesn't say who did it. When you **do** want to say it, put **by + the doer** after the verb. **by = oleh**: *Novel ini ditulis **oleh** Pramoedya* → *This novel was written **by** Pramoedya.*

**The trap:** don't use **from** here. **from = dari** tells you where something **comes from**: *a letter from Budi* (surat dari Budi), *coffee from Aceh*. **by** tells you **who did the action**: *a letter written by Budi*. So 'written from Pramoedya' is wrong.

After **by**, a pronoun takes its object form (the form after a verb): **by me, by him, by her, by us, by them** (not 'by she').

id.text:
Biasanya kalimat passive tidak menyebut siapa pelakunya. Kalau kamu **ingin** menyebutnya, taruh **by + pelaku** setelah kata kerjanya. **by = oleh**: *Novel ini ditulis **oleh** Pramoedya* → *This novel was written **by** Pramoedya.*

**Jebakannya:** jangan pakai **from** di sini. **from = dari** menunjukkan **asal** sesuatu: *a letter from Budi* (surat dari Budi), *coffee from Aceh*. **by** menunjukkan **siapa yang melakukan tindakan**: *a letter written by Budi*. Jadi 'written from Pramoedya' itu salah.

Setelah **by**, kata ganti memakai bentuk objek (bentuk yang dipakai setelah kata kerja): **by me, by him, by her, by us, by them** (bukan 'by she').

blocks.text: **made by** or **made in**? **by** = who made it (*made by my grandmother*, *made by Toyota*), **in** = the place (*made in Indonesia*, *made in Japan*).

id.text: **made by** atau **made in**? **by** = siapa yang membuat (*made by my grandmother*, *made by Toyota*), **in** = tempatnya (*made in Indonesia*, *made in Japan*).

blocks.prompt: The novel Bumi Manusia was written ___ Pramoedya Ananta Toer.
blocks.explain: The doer of a passive comes after by (= oleh). from (= dari) is for where something comes from, and with is for a tool or a person you do something together with.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The novel Bumi Manusia was written ___ Pramoedya Ananta Toer.
id.explain: Pelaku dalam kalimat passive ditaruh setelah by (= oleh). from (= dari) untuk asal sesuatu, dan with untuk alat atau orang yang melakukan sesuatu bersamamu.

blocks.text:
English uses the active most of the time. Choose the **passive** when the **thing** is more important than the person:
- the doer is **unknown**: *My phone was stolen.* (nobody knows who)
- the doer is **obvious**: *The rubbish is collected on Mondays.* (by the rubbish collectors, of course)
- the doer is **unimportant**, or the **thing is the topic**: *Rice is grown in many parts of Java.* *Borobudur was built in the 9th century.* This is common in news, notices, instructions and descriptions of how things are made.

Then you usually **leave out by**: *by someone*, *by people* or *by farmers* adds nothing.

**Use the active** when the doer matters, especially when it's **you**. Indonesian often says *Bajunya sudah saya cuci* or *Kopinya saya buat*, but English sounds strange with 'by me': say **I've washed the clothes** (not 'The clothes were washed by me').

id.text:
Bahasa Inggris lebih sering memakai kalimat aktif. Pilih **passive** kalau **bendanya** lebih penting daripada orangnya:
- pelakunya **tidak diketahui**: *My phone was stolen.* (tidak ada yang tahu siapa)
- pelakunya **sudah jelas**: *The rubbish is collected on Mondays.* (tentu oleh petugas sampah)
- pelakunya **tidak penting**, atau **bendanya yang jadi topik**: *Rice is grown in many parts of Java.* *Borobudur was built in the 9th century.* Ini sering dipakai di berita, pengumuman, petunjuk, dan penjelasan tentang cara membuat sesuatu.

Kalau begitu, **by biasanya tidak disebut**: *by someone*, *by people* atau *by farmers* tidak menambah informasi.

**Pakai kalimat aktif** kalau pelakunya penting, terutama kalau pelakunya **kamu sendiri**. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kita sering bilang *Bajunya sudah saya cuci* atau *Kopinya saya buat*, tapi dalam bahasa Inggris 'by me' terdengar aneh: ucapkan **I've washed the clothes** (bukan 'The clothes were washed by me').

rows.en: My laptop was stolen last night.
The rubbish is collected on Mondays.
rows.note: obvious doer · rubbish is British; Americans say trash or garbage

id.note: pelakunya sudah jelas · rubbish itu British; orang Amerika bilang trash atau garbage

rows.en: Most of Indonesia's coffee is grown in Sumatra.
rows.id: Sebagian besar kopi Indonesia ditanam di Sumatra.

rows.en: Rina organised the event.
rows.note: the doer is the news → active · organised is British, organized is American

id.note: pelakunya yang jadi berita → aktif · organised itu ejaan British, organized ejaan Amerika

blocks.text: Indonesian uses its passive (*di-*, *saya buat*) much more than English uses the passive. A quick test: is the doer **you** or the important part of the news? → **active**. Is the doer unknown, obvious or not interesting? → **passive**, usually without by.

id.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai kalimat pasif (*di-*, *saya buat*) jauh lebih sering daripada bahasa Inggris. Tes cepat: apakah pelakunya **kamu sendiri** atau bagian penting dari beritanya? → **aktif**. Apakah pelakunya tidak diketahui, sudah jelas atau tidak menarik? → **passive**, biasanya tanpa by.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is the most natural in a travel guide?
options: Rice is grown in many parts of Java by farmers.
Many parts of Java grow rice by farmers.
Rice is grown in many parts of Java.
blocks.explain: Rice is the topic and the doer (farmers) is obvious, so use the passive without by. 'by farmers' adds nothing, and 'Many parts of Java grow rice by farmers' mixes the active with by.

id.prompt: Kalimat mana yang paling wajar di buku panduan wisata?
id.explain: Padi adalah topiknya dan pelakunya (petani) sudah jelas, jadi pakai passive tanpa by. 'by farmers' tidak menambah informasi, dan 'Many parts of Java grow rice by farmers' mencampur kalimat aktif dengan by.

My phone was stolen! Hari ini kamu belajar membentuknya dengan is/are/was/were + bentuk ketiga, menyebut pelakunya dengan by, dan tahu kapan passive lebih tepat. Pemanasan: kamu lahir di mana? (I was born in…: kamu sudah memakai passive!)
suggestedQuestions: Kenapa 'The office cleaned every day' salah?
Apakah 'di-' dalam bahasa Indonesia sama dengan passive dalam bahasa Inggris?
Kapan aku perlu 'by', dan kenapa bukan 'from'?
Kenapa 'The coffee was made by me' terdengar aneh?

assessment.pas-1: Lengkapi dengan present simple passive dari 'sell': KRL tickets ___ at every station.
assessment.pas-2: Lengkapi dengan past simple passive dari 'send': The invoices ___ to the client yesterday.
assessment.pas-3: Perbaiki kesalahannya (ini fakta tentang sekarang): Our office cleaned every evening.
assessment.pas-4: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Inggris dengan 'by': Foto ini diambil oleh Budi.
assessment.pas-5: Perbaiki kesalahannya: The new company logo was designed from Dimas.
assessment.pas-6: Tidak ada yang tahu siapa pelakunya. Tulis ulang dalam bentuk passive, tanpa pelakunya: Someone stole my wallet on the KRL.
assessment.pas-7: Kalimat ini terdengar aneh karena pelakunya 'me'. Tulis ulang dalam bentuk aktif: The coffee was made by me this morning.
